original_text: Washington, D.C. — The U.S. Treasury Department has formally declared the federal government insolvent, according to its Fiscal Year 2025 consolidated financial statements released on March 23, 2026. The report lists $6.06 trillion in total assets and $47.78 trillion in total liabilities, leaving a net negative position of $41.72 trillion. When off-balance-sheet obligations such as Social Security and Medicare are included, total federal obligations exceed $136 trillion, about five times U.S. annual GDP. The Treasury summary states that the government’s liabilities now exceed its assets by an unprecedented margin. Economists Steve Hanke and David Walker wrote that the Treasury’s own numbers confirm insolvency. The report was signed by the Treasury Secretary and transmitted to Congress.
